title: Wind Damage and Wear on a Texas Roof
description: Lifted tabs and a creased shingle are wind. Bald spots and curl from years of sun are wear. Insurers pay one of those.
html:
A storm claim dies in one sentence: “that is wear and tear.” Sometimes the adjuster is right. Sometimes the wind lifted a course last night and the sun has been working on the roof for fifteen years besides. You need to tell those apart before you argue.

What wind does

Wind gets under a tab and bends it. A fresh lift often shows a clean crease, unsealed adhesive, and fasteners that are shiny where the shingle pulled. On the edges and rakes, tabs are missing in a row, not in a random pepper. Debris from the yard may be jammed under the remaining shingles. That pattern lines up with a date you can name.

What age does

Age curls the edges slowly, cracks the asphalt in alligator lines, and thins the granules across a whole slope, especially the south and west. The adhesive dried out years ago. Nothing about it points at last Tuesday. A policy is built to pay for a sudden event, not for a roof that reached the end of its life during a windy month.

Both can be true on the same house. The south slope can be worn out while the north slope took a real lift. A fair scope says so. A contractor who calls all of it wind, or an adjuster who calls all of it age, is not looking.

How we write it down

One slope can be both

We mark it that way in the photos: wind on the north edge, age across the south field. You can repair the wind and plan the worn slope for later, or replace the roof because the worn slope will not match a repair and you do not want two colors. Both are honest. Calling the worn slope wind, so a policy pays for age, is how claims get denied and how contractors get a reputation. We will not write that report.

We photograph the crease, the sealant strip, and a worn slope next to a damaged one, and we put dates on the photos. That packet is what you hand the carrier. The insurance claim walkthrough explains the rest of the sequence, including depreciation. If you want us on the roof before you open anything, request a free inspection or call (281) 541-0027.
